subject: URGENT: Production 5xx/429 spike impacting Atlas Health — immediate mitigation required
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
Cc: atlas-ops@atlashealth.com
Date: 2027-05-30T09:41:00Z
Subject: High error rate — 5xx/429 spike since 09:20 UTC (Zendesk #8472)

Camila —

We're seeing a major surge of 5xx and 429 responses from the Redwood API hitting our checkout flow starting ~09:20 UTC. Impacting ~18% of user checkouts across regions. Our SREs captured several request IDs (sample below) and a short span of traces showing repeated retries from our SDK. We opened Zendesk ticket #8472 and attached logs.

Sample request IDs: 3c9b2a, 3c9b2f, 3c9b34
Symptoms: timeouts followed by 502/504 and then 429s. Latency for successful requests also jumped from ~150ms to ~2.4s.

Immediate asks: can you confirm if there was a deployment, model change, or config flip on your side? We need either a rollback or a mitigation (throttle/route to fallback) ASAP — our largest customer is being directly affected and our CS team is getting inundated.

Please escalate to engineering and let us know ETA for mitigation.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Engineering Ops
Atlas Health

Attachments: zendesk-8472.log (attached to ticket)
From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai

Liam — thanks for the heads up and for the sample IDs. I'm standing this up as an immediate incident.

Short term: I'm asking SRE to run the emergency playbook now (disable client-side retries for your integration where possible, apply per-tenant throttling, and enable a fallback model variant). Rishi — can you confirm which mitigations we can apply within the next 10–15 minutes and whether there was any deployment at 09:15–09:35?

I'll keep this thread as the single source of truth and will schedule a 30m war room in 10 minutes. Jonas — flagging for exec awareness; this touches a large renewal in Q3.

Camila Reyes
Head of Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)
camila.reyes@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0183

Attachments: (I will upload a summary once SRE confirms)
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T09:54:30Z
Subject: Re: High error rate — 5xx/429 spike since 09:20 UTC (initial analysis)

Quick diagnostics:
- No deployment recorded in the window 09:15–09:35 UTC on the hosted fleet.
- We see a sudden retention of outstanding requests in the frontend queue (~4x normal) and a correlated spike in KV cache evictions.
- Many of the 5xx traces show worker process OOMs followed by upstream 502/504. Separately, 429s are coming from our rate limiter after queue saturation.
- Notable signal: a pattern of rapid client retries from the Atlas SDK (backoff misconfigured to max 10x with minimal jitter). That produced retry amplification under transient latency which amplified queue pressure.

Immediate actions taken (09:50–09:54):
1) Applied per-tenant soft throttle for atlas-health to cap concurrency at 60 rps (temporary).
2) Enabled fallback model variant (lower-memory quantized build) for atlas-health traffic to reduce worker memory pressure.
3) Disabled auto-scaling burst for a subset of the pool to stop oscillation while we observe.

Follow-ups we recommend in the next 3 hours:
- Short-term: implement a server-side retry-quarantine (reject obvious retry floods with 429+Retry-After instrumentation) and update alert thresholds for queue length and cache eviction rates.
- Medium-term: update the onboarding SDK docs to highlight recommended backoff jitter and default limits; offer a hotfix release for Atlas.
- Long-term: add per-tenant circuit-breaker and refine autoscaler cooldown logic to prevent thrashing.

I uploaded a quick summary and the throttle patch to the shared drive. I'll keep watching metrics and will report back in 15 minutes.

Rishi Malhotra
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: camila.reyes@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: grace.oconnor@redwood.ai, liam@atlashealth.com

We should block a 1-hour postmortem slot tomorrow; include SRE, platform, SDK, and account team.

— Jonas
From: camila.reyes@redwood.ai
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@atlashealth.com>
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, jonas.weber@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-05-30T10:18:10Z
Subject: Re: High error rate — mitigation applied, can you verify

Liam —

We've applied the temporary mitigations Rishi listed (per-tenant throttle, fallback variant enabled, and a temporary throttle patch). Early telemetry shows 5xx rate dropping from 18% -> 4% in the first 10 minutes and 429s stabilizing; tail latency trending back toward normal. I've attached a short CSV with the 30-minute pre/post sample (logs_summary-20270530.csv).

Notes on user-visible impact: fallback model reduces token horizon slightly in long context scenarios; short, per-request latencies improved. We'll revert to normal routing once the system has been stable for 60 continuous minutes.

Next steps:
- 10:30 UTC: 15-minute check-in (war room). Invite: camila,re; rishi; atlas ops.
- 14:00 UTC: post-incident sync and customer-facing postmortem outline.
- Action items assigned: Rishi (detailed postmortem RCA), SDK team (hotfix for backoff defaults), Account (Camila) to draft credit proposal if requested.

Please confirm if you still see errors. Thank you for rapid communication.

Camila Reyes
Head of Strategic Accounts (Redwood Inference)

Attachments: logs_summary-20270530.csv, temporary-throttle-config.patch

Metrics are much improved. 5xx down to ~2.1% and 429s no longer throttling legitimate requests. Checkout success rate returning to baseline. Thanks for the quick mitigation — Atlas Ops is requesting the following:

1) A formal postmortem with timeline and root cause within 48 hours.
2) Confirmation on whether this will count as an SLA incident and credit eligibility (we'll await your account team's proposal).
3) A scheduled SDK sync next week to get the recommended backoff hotfix into our release branch.

We're open to a short renewal discussion if Redwood can demonstrate a clear mitigation plan and runbook changes that reduce recurrence risk. Meeting looks good at 14:00 UTC.

— Liam
